extracted.intended_audience: neuroscience researchers and principal investigators applying for NIH BRAIN Initiative funding (technology developers, clinicians, resource centers, and institutional partners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing applications to BRAIN Initiative Notices of Funding Opportunities (NOFOs) across technology, translational, reagent production, data archive, and equity-focused partnership programs. Covers expected aims, scopes, and required features for competitive proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: New concepts and early-stage technology development
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek applications for unique and innovative technologies that are in an even earlier stage of development than that sought in other FOAs, including new and untested ideas that are in the initial stages of conceptualization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals may include calculations, simulations, computational models, or other mathematical techniques demonstrating theoretical capability for large-scale recording or manipulation; building and testing phantoms, prototypes, in-vitro or bench-top models to validate underlying theoretical assumptions in preparation for future FOAs aimed at testing in animal models. Clinical trials not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting equity through technology partnerships with resource-limited institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase impact by targeted dissemination and integration of validated BRAIN Initiative tools to investigators at institutions that historically have not been major recipients of NIH support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards support PIs at resource-limited institutions (RLIs) who pair with BRAIN technologists to facilitate training and adoption; goals include two-way knowledge transfer between PI and technologist and increased participation of PIs at RLIs in BRAIN-relevant research. Clinical trials not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and validation of cell- and circuit-specific tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage applications that will develop and validate novel tools to facilitate the detailed analysis of complex circuits and provide insights into cellular interactions that underlie brain function; tools should inform and/or exploit cell-type and/or circuit-level specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans for validating the utility of the tool/technology are an essential feature of a successful application. Development of genetic and non-genetic delivery tools encouraged. Tools usable across multiple species/model organisms are highly desired. Applications that break through existing technical barriers to substantially improve current capabilities are encouraged. Clinical trials not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational development of next-generation human CNS devices (UG3/UH3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage investigators to pursue translational activities and small clinical studies to advance development of therapeutic and diagnostic devices for nervous or neuromuscular system disorders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported activities include implementation of clinical prototype devices, non-clinical safety and efficacy testing, design verification and validation, obtaining an IDE for a Significant Risk (SR) study, and a subsequent small clinical study. The program is milestone-driven, operates as a cooperative agreement, and will involve NIH program staff negotiating the final project plan and monitoring progress. Clinical trial optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small clinical studies to advance device design and function (UH3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support small clinical trials to obtain critical information necessary to advance recording and/or stimulating devices to treat CNS disorders and better understand the human brain (e.g., Early Feasibility Study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical studies may be acute/short-term procedures deemed Non-Significant Risk (NSR) by IRB, or Significant Risk (SR) studies requiring an FDA IDE (e.g., chronic implants). Trials should provide data that cannot be practically obtained through additional non-clinical assessments due to device novelty or intended use. Leverage BRAIN Public-Private Partnership (BRAIN PPP) device availability where appropriate; expect devices' existing safety/utility data may enable IRB NSR or FDA IDE without significant additional non-clinical data. Clinical trial optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Next-generation sensor and behavior synchronization for computational models (U01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit development of next generation sensor and bioelectronic device development that will synchronize with brain recordings to generate new computational models of behavior in human and animal models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the current lack of quantitative approaches and models to understand complexity of behavior in naturalistic settings. Emphasize sensor development to acquire synchronized data with brain recordings to build computational models. Clinical trial optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish reagent production and distribution facilities at MSIs/IDeA institutions (U24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support establishment of facilities at minority-serving institutions (MSIs) and Institutional Development Award (IDeA)-eligible institutions for scaled production and distribution of brain cell type-specific access and manipulation reagents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reagents developed in pilot projects under the Armamentarium project will be manufactured and distributed; awardees will work with other Armamentarium awardees and the neuroscience community to optimize use. Reagent types may include viral vectors, nucleic acid constructs, and nanoparticles for selective access/manipulation across vertebrate species. Facilities should contribute to production and broad distribution for neuroscience users. Clinical trial not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-accessible data archives with appropriate standards (R24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop web-accessible data archives to capture, store, and curate data related to BRAIN Initiative activities, creating a community resource to advance research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archives should work with the research community to incorporate tools that allow users to analyze and visualize data (creation of such tools is not part of this NOFO). Data should be described using appropriate standards (creating standards themselves is not part of this NOFO). Aim for broadly available, accessible resources with appropriate standards and summary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclinical proof-of-concept to reach first-in-human readiness (R18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitate translation of novel recording and modulation technologies from proof-of-concept up to the stage of readiness for first-in-human (FIH) studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technologies may incorporate any signal modality (electrical, optical, magnetic, acoustic, or combinations). Diverse, team-based applications integrating appropriate expertise are encouraged. Activities should position technologies for eventual FIH testing. Clinical trials not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and distribution facilities for brain cell type-specific reagents (U24 — earlier FOA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support scaled reagent production and distribution facilities involving technologies to access brain cell types, encouraging broad and diverse neuroscientist use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Armamentarium for Brain Cell Access transformative project. Efforts should produce and distribute gene transfer, gene regulation, and genome engineering reagents for genetically tractable and less tractable systems (including primates and human tissue) relevant for future translational efforts. Reagents should be those designed and validated under other Armamentarium NOFOs. Clinical trial not allowed.
